guides.definition: A variable annotation follows the binding name and is checked statically. The annotation is erased before JavaScript executes.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: A runtime expression assignable to the selected type.

examples.title: Annotate a number
examples.code:
const answer: number = 42;
console.log(answer);
examples.explanation: TypeScript checks that 42 is assignable to number, then Node.js executes the emitted JavaScript value.

guides.definition: Function annotations document and check what callers may pass and what the function promises to return.

parameters.name: argumentType
parameters.description: The type accepted by the function.

parameters.name: returnType
parameters.description: The type produced by the function.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: An expression assignable to the return type.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: A value used for the example call.

examples.title: Type a numeric function
examples.explanation: The function accepts and returns numbers, so the call produces 42.

guides.definition: An interface names a required object shape. TypeScript uses structural compatibility, so a value matches when it supplies the required members.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: A value assignable to the property type.

examples.title: Describe a user
examples.explanation: The object satisfies User because it contains the required string property.

guides.definition: A type alias can name primitives, object shapes, unions, tuples, and other type expressions. It exists only during type analysis.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The type assigned to the alias.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: A value assignable to the alias.

examples.title: Name an identifier type
examples.explanation: Identifier can hold either a string or number, and the sample uses its number member.

guides.definition: A union joins member types with the vertical bar. Code may use only behavior common to every member until it narrows the value.

parameters.name: members
parameters.description: Types joined with a vertical bar.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: A value matching one union member.

examples.title: Allow text or numbers
examples.explanation: The string literal is valid because string is one member of Result.

guides.definition: Control-flow analysis narrows a union inside branches whose runtime checks prove which member is present.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: A string or number expression to narrow.

examples.title: Narrow a number
examples.explanation: The false branch knows value is a number and safely calls toFixed.

guides.definition: A type parameter acts as a placeholder chosen by each call. Returning the same parameter preserves the caller's exact type.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The concrete type supplied for T.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: A value assignable to the type argument.

examples.title: Preserve a string type
examples.explanation: T is string for this call, so the return value remains a string.

guides.definition: A readonly modifier protects a property from reassignment in TypeScript. It does not freeze the JavaScript object at runtime.

examples.title: Protect a configuration mode
examples.explanation: The initial value is valid, while later assignment to mode would be a type error.

guides.definition: A question mark makes a property optional. Reading it produces the declared type combined with undefined, so optional chaining or narrowing is appropriate.

parameters.name: property
parameters.description: The property that may be absent.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: Properties placed inside the sample object.

parameters.name: fallback
parameters.description: A string expression used when the property is absent.

examples.title: Handle an absent nickname
examples.explanation: Optional chaining returns undefined for the missing property and nullish coalescing supplies the fallback.

guides.definition: A discriminated union gives each object variant a common property with a distinct literal value. Checking that property narrows the remaining fields.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: An object matching one Result variant.

examples.title: Handle a success state
examples.explanation: Checking kind narrows result to the success variant before reading value.

guides.definition: An implements clause checks a class against a structural contract. The class still needs explicit property and method annotations where desired.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: A string passed to the constructor.

examples.title: Implement Named
examples.explanation: Person supplies the required name property and adds a typed describe method.

guides.definition: The satisfies operator checks that an expression is assignable to a type while preserving the expression's more specific inferred properties.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: A string literal accepted by Channel.

examples.title: Validate configuration
examples.explanation: The object is checked against the contract while config.channel retains its specific literal information.

guides.definition: keyof produces a union of known property names. Combining it with indexed access lets a generic function return the exact type associated with a selected key.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: A string literal key from the sample object.

examples.title: Read the theme
examples.explanation: The key is constrained to theme or fontSize, and the selected theme value is inferred as string.

guides.definition: A const assertion prevents widening of literal values and gives arrays or object properties readonly inferred types. It does not freeze the runtime value.

examples.title: Preserve route literals
examples.code:
const route = { method: "GET", path: "/status" } as const;
console.log(route.method, route.path);
examples.explanation: The inferred method and path remain their exact literal values rather than widening to string.

guides.definition: An async function returns a Promise whose type argument describes the eventual value. await unwraps that value inside another async operation.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: A numeric value resolved by the promise.

examples.title: Await a number
examples.explanation: The promise resolves to number, and await produces a number inside the async function.

guides.definition: An intersection joins types with ampersands. The resulting type contains the compatible requirements of every member and is useful for composing orthogonal capabilities.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the combined contract.

examples.title: Combine identity and display data
examples.explanation: The object contains the required members from both sides of the intersection.

guides.definition: Literal types preserve exact values in the type system. Joining them in a union creates an enumerable domain that editors can autocomplete and the checker can exhaustively analyze.

parameters.name: members
parameters.description: Literal types joined with vertical bars.

examples.title: Represent a direction
examples.explanation: Direction accepts only its two declared string literals.

guides.definition: A tuple is an array type with a known sequence of element types. Labels improve readability without changing runtime behavior.

parameters.name: firstValue
parameters.description: A value for the first position.

parameters.name: secondValue
parameters.description: A value for the second position.

examples.title: Create a coordinate tuple
examples.explanation: Each tuple position is checked independently while the runtime value remains an array.

guides.definition: The readonly modifier prevents mutating methods and indexed assignment during type checking. It does not freeze the runtime array.

parameters.name: firstValue
parameters.description: A value for the first position.

parameters.name: secondValue
parameters.description: A value for the second position.

examples.title: Declare a readonly pair
examples.explanation: The pair can be read normally, but assignment to either indexed position would fail type checking.

guides.definition: An extends clause on a type parameter limits accepted types. Code inside the generic declaration may safely use members guaranteed by that constraint.

parameters.name: constraint
parameters.description: The minimum object shape required of T.

parameters.name: property
parameters.description: A member guaranteed by the constraint.

examples.title: Accept any value with a length
examples.explanation: The constraint permits length access while retaining the caller's concrete string type for T.

guides.definition: A default type parameter follows an equals sign and makes that type argument optional when inference cannot select a more specific type.

parameters.name: defaultType
parameters.description: The type used when no argument is provided.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: A value matching the default instantiation.

examples.title: Default a container to strings
examples.explanation: Omitting the type argument makes this Container equivalent to Container<string>.

guides.definition: Indexed access uses bracket notation in a type position. A union of keys produces the union of their corresponding property types.

parameters.name: resultType
parameters.description: The alias for the selected property type.

parameters.name: keyType
parameters.description: A property-name literal or key union.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: A value assignable to the selected type.

examples.title: Extract an identifier property type
examples.explanation: User["id"] resolves to number without duplicating the property's declaration.

guides.definition: TypeScript's typeof type operator refers to the checker-known type of a value. It is distinct from JavaScript's runtime typeof expression.

parameters.name: sourceName
parameters.description: The value whose type is captured.

parameters.name: typeName
parameters.description: The alias receiving the inferred type.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: A value matching the captured type.

examples.title: Reuse an inferred configuration shape
examples.explanation: Configuration stays synchronized with the shape inferred for defaults.

guides.definition: A conditional type has the form T extends U ? X : Y. When T is a naked type parameter, unions may distribute through the condition member by member.

parameters.name: condition
parameters.description: The type T is tested against.

parameters.name: trueType
parameters.description: The type selected when T is assignable.

parameters.name: sampleInput
parameters.description: The type used to instantiate T.

parameters.name: sampleValue
parameters.description: A value matching the selected result.

examples.title: Classify a type
examples.explanation: Because string extends string, the conditional type selects the text literal.

guides.definition: The infer keyword declares a type variable in the true branch's match pattern. It is commonly used to extract function results, promise values, and tuple elements.

parameters.name: functionName
parameters.description: A declared function whose result is extracted.

examples.title: Extract a function return type
examples.explanation: infer captures the return component of the function type as R.

guides.definition: A mapped type uses an in clause over a key union, commonly keyof T. Modifiers can be added or removed while each property's value type is retained or transformed.

parameters.name: wrapper
parameters.description: A generic wrapper applied to each property.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: A value matching the mapped result.

examples.title: Make every property a promise
examples.explanation: The mapped type preserves the id key while wrapping its number value type in Promise.

guides.definition: Mapped key remapping combines keyof, template literal types, and an as clause. Mapping a key to never removes that property.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: Text prepended to each generated key.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: The object keys and values to remap.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: A value using the remapped key.

examples.title: Generate getter-style keys
examples.explanation: The name key is remapped to getName and retains its string value type.

guides.definition: Template literal types use the runtime template-literal shape in type positions. Union interpolation forms the cross-product of possible strings.

parameters.name: members
parameters.description: String literals joined in a union.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: Text placed before each interpolated member.

parameters.name: suffix
parameters.description: Text placed after each interpolated member.

examples.title: Generate change event names
examples.explanation: Interpolation and Capitalize generate one event-name literal for each Field member.

guides.definition: A return type such as value is string is a type predicate. Callers narrow the tested value when the function returns true.

parameters.name: targetType
parameters.description: The type proven by a true result.

parameters.name: condition
parameters.description: A boolean expression that validates the value.

parameters.name: use
parameters.description: An expression valid for the narrowed type.

examples.title: Narrow an unknown value to string
examples.explanation: Inside the branch, the predicate narrows value from unknown to string.

guides.definition: An asserts return type models a function that cannot return normally unless its stated condition holds. Assertions are useful at validation boundaries.

parameters.name: targetType
parameters.description: The type established after a successful call.

parameters.name: condition
parameters.description: The condition that validates the value.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: The expression used for the thrown error.

parameters.name: use
parameters.description: An expression valid after the assertion.

examples.title: Assert that input is text
examples.explanation: A normal return proves value is string for all following statements in the scope.

guides.definition: When the left operand is a property-name literal, TypeScript narrows the right operand to union members that may contain that property.

parameters.name: leftType
parameters.description: The union member containing the tested property.

parameters.name: property
parameters.description: The property name checked with in.

parameters.name: leftUse
parameters.description: An expression valid for the first member.

parameters.name: rightUse
parameters.description: An expression valid for the alternate member.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: A value matching one union member.

examples.title: Distinguish a path from a URL
examples.explanation: The property test narrows the first branch to the object containing path.

guides.definition: An instanceof expression checks an object's prototype chain. TypeScript uses a successful check to narrow the value to the constructor's instance type.

parameters.name: leftUse
parameters.description: An expression valid for the class instance.

parameters.name: rightUse
parameters.description: An expression valid for the other member.

examples.title: Distinguish a Date from text
examples.explanation: The true branch knows value is a Date and exposes Date methods.

guides.definition: unknown accepts every value like any, but disallows arbitrary operations until control-flow analysis or an assertion establishes a narrower type.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: The value entering an untrusted boundary.

parameters.name: condition
parameters.description: A runtime check proving a useful type.

parameters.name: use
parameters.description: An expression valid after the check.

examples.title: Safely inspect unknown input
examples.code:
const value: unknown = "typed";
if (typeof value === "string") console.log(value.toUpperCase());
examples.explanation: The runtime check is required before string behavior is available.

guides.definition: never represents values that cannot occur. Assigning a switch remainder to never verifies that earlier cases handled every discriminant member.

parameters.name: members
parameters.description: Literal types handled by the switch.

parameters.name: cases
parameters.description: A case for every declared member.

examples.title: Require every state case
examples.explanation: If State gains another member, the default assignment stops compiling until that member is handled.

guides.definition: Overload signatures are visible to callers but erased from output. The implementation signature must accommodate every overload and is not itself callable from the outside.

parameters.name: implementation
parameters.description: An expression compatible with both results.

examples.title: Overload an identity normalizer
examples.explanation: Callers receive a precise result type for each accepted input shape.

guides.definition: A call signature is written without an arrow inside an object type. It is useful for JavaScript functions that carry configuration or metadata properties.

parameters.name: property
parameters.description: A property carried by the function value.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: The expression returned by the function.

parameters.name: propertyValue
parameters.description: The metadata value assigned to the callable.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: A value accepted by the call signature.

examples.title: Create a labeled formatter
examples.explanation: The function satisfies both the callable signature and the label property requirement.

guides.definition: A construct signature begins with new and describes constructor parameters plus the resulting instance type. It enables factories that accept class-like values.

parameters.name: parameter
parameters.description: The instance value initialized by the constructor.

parameters.name: parameterType
parameters.description: The type accepted by the constructor.

parameters.name: className
parameters.description: A concrete class satisfying the signature.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: A value passed to the constructor.

examples.title: Accept a class in a factory
examples.explanation: Item's constructor matches the construct signature and can be passed as a value to the factory.

guides.definition: An index signature constrains property values accessed by string, number, symbol, or a permitted template-pattern key type.

parameters.name: valueType
parameters.description: The value returned for each key.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: An object satisfying the index signature.

parameters.name: sampleKey
parameters.description: A key used to read the object.

examples.title: Map names to numeric scores
examples.explanation: Every string-named property in Scores must hold a number.

guides.definition: Interface declarations participate in TypeScript declaration merging. Non-function members must be unique or have matching types, while overload groups are combined.

parameters.name: firstProperty
parameters.description: A member from the first declaration.

parameters.name: secondProperty
parameters.description: A member from the second declaration.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: An object satisfying the merged interface.

examples.title: Merge dimension members
examples.explanation: The merged Dimensions contract requires both width and height.

guides.definition: A generic interface declares type parameters after its name. Each instantiation substitutes concrete types throughout the interface's members.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The concrete value type for this instance.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: An object satisfying the generic interface.
parameters.defaultValue: { value: 42, map(transform) { return { value: transform(this.value), map: this.map }; } }

examples.title: Create a typed box
examples.explanation: Instantiating Box<number> makes its value member a number.

guides.definition: A fake first parameter named this exists only for checking. It prevents a function from being called with an incompatible receiver.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: An expression using the typed receiver.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: An object satisfying the receiver contract.

examples.title: Require a counter receiver
examples.explanation: The this parameter is erased, but call must provide a receiver with a numeric value.

guides.definition: A question mark after a parameter name adds undefined to its effective type. Optional parameters must follow required parameters unless a default handles omission.

examples.title: Greet with an optional name
examples.explanation: The function accepts a string or omission and explicitly handles the undefined case.

guides.definition: A rest parameter may use a tuple type, including optional and named elements. Calls are checked as though the tuple elements were separate parameters.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: An expression using the tuple arguments.

examples.title: Format a labeled value
examples.explanation: The rest array retains a fixed two-position tuple type at the call site and in the body.

guides.definition: Variadic tuple types allow generic spreads in tuple positions. They model operations such as concatenation, partial application, and argument forwarding precisely.

parameters.name: right
parameters.description: The tuple appended after the first.

examples.title: Concatenate two typed tuples
examples.explanation: The result retains the ordered string, number, and boolean element types.

guides.definition: A brand is a TypeScript modeling convention rather than a runtime feature. A unique marker property makes otherwise identical structural types incompatible after validation or construction.

parameters.name: brandLiteral
parameters.description: A unique literal used only by the checker.

examples.title: Brand a numeric user identifier
examples.explanation: The brand exists only in the type system while the runtime value remains a number.
